newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank sets no repo operation on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank sets no repo operation on Friday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold any repo operation on Friday as crown liquidity was sufficient to allow the local banking sector to meet minimum reserve requirements (PMR).

"Even though 2.0 billion crowns leave the market in a maturing repo tender, the banks start this reserves period with PMR fulfilment over 100 percent so there is no need to add additional liquidity through repo tenders," said Peter Andresic, Head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department.

The central bank's tight control over the money market has kept the local interbank market slightly short of crown liquidity over the past 10 weeks and the banking sector has failed to meet its PMR in the last five consecutive periods.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector exceeded its minimum reserves requirements, set at 36.583 billion crowns, by 0.63 percent at the end of the last PMR perdiod on July 31.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks totals 36.817 billion crowns for the current period ending August 15.
The central bank monitors market liquidity on a daily basis and decides each morning whether to hold any open market operations.

The last NBS repo operation was the Wednesday's one-week repo adding 1.5 billion crowns into the local money market with an average rate falling to 15.55 percent from 16.30 percent in a similar repo on Tuesday.
